Genomic epidemiology for public health outbreak investigations

Microbial Population Genomics and Phylogenetics

Genome sequencing is now a routine part of outbreak investigations. This training covers how to turn microbial genomes into evidence for public health action: identifying and typing organisms, measuring how closely isolates are related, building and reading phylogenetic trees, and interpreting the results alongside epidemiological data.

The material is organized into six connected sections. Each one pairs short lectures with hands-on activities that use real public data and the command-line tools used in public health laboratories.

Developed by the Western Region AMD Leads for laboratories in the Western Region, and open to anyone working in public health genomics.

Course sections

01 Foundations of Microbial Population Genomics Microbial evolution, mutation, recombination, population structure, genetic diversity, and species delineation. Content forthcoming 02 Taxonomic Classification and Genomic Subtyping Genome-based species identification, MLST, k-mer-based methods, and other microbial typing approaches. 3 lectures · 3 activities 03 High-Resolution Genomic Relatedness Core genome MLST (cgMLST), core-SNP analysis, genomic distance, clustering, and analytical limitations. Content forthcoming 04 Phylogenetic Methods and Tree Building Evolutionary models, tree-building methods, rooting, branch lengths, support values, and tree interpretation. Content forthcoming 05 Interpreting Phylogenomic Evidence in Outbreak Investigations Genomic clusters, background diversity, epidemiological integration, uncertainty, and transmission inference limitations. Content forthcoming 06 Integrated Genomic Epidemiology Case Studies Applying typing, genomic relatedness, phylogenetics, and epidemiological evidence to outbreak investigation scenarios. Content forthcoming
